v1.feedback: The normal-based inflation is the right move for 'marshmallow' but inflate=2.8*mallowOffset risks bloating Lucy into a featureless blob at full uMallow — cap it around 1.5 or add a curvature-dependent term so concavities (face, drapery folds) inflate less, preserving the silhouette that makes Lucy worth using. The toasted-gold radial gradient is a nice touch but purely radial from origin — tie it to local curvature or convexity instead so tips and ridges toast first, which reads more like actual caramelization. The upward y-drift (0.6 units) competes with the orbit camera's fixed lookAt(0,0,0), slowly pushing the torso out of center; either shift lookAt.y up with uMallow or drop the drift.

v2.feedback: The idea lands — Lucy inflates along convex normals into a puffy marshmallow silhouette, and the ivory-to-golden-brown toasting gradient is a genuinely clever tonal swerve that reads in seconds. The periodic squish with elastic overshoot adds playful physicality. Two things to sharpen: the convexity proxy (dot of normal with radial direction) is crude and will misfire on Lucy's concave drapery folds, producing uneven inflation — a Laplacian smoothing pass or pre-baked curvature attribute would give cleaner puff. Second, the slow orbit camera never brings us close enough to appreciate the toasting detail or particle softness; a tighter framing or a brief dolly-in during the squish would sell the marshmallow scale better. Palette is restrained and warm, motion earns its keep — solid surprise-mode entry.
